parsed.title: Discussion on AI tools for job search and software development

topics.title: AI for job searching and resume automation

claims.text: The author is preparing for a full‑time job search and considers automating PDF resume generation for specific vacancies.
They plan to set up OpenClaw to find vacancies, generate resumes and cover letters after their startup closes.
In 2026, adding many AI‑related skills (Cursor, Claude Code, LLM, RAG, Embeddings, etc.) is necessary to avoid being filtered out by recruiters.
The acceleration of development tools started in 2025, with market‑ready, though expensive, solutions becoming available.
Candidate search by keyword is becoming increasingly detached from reality.
The author expects the recruiting profession to become obsolete.
AI‑generated code can drastically lower the entry barrier to programming but may produce insecure, unoptimized queries.
AI‑generated code can lead to poor quality implementations that break projects and are hard to review.

topics.title: AI impact on software development speed

claims.text: Using GPT to generate SQL joins and other code significantly speeds up development.
The discussed projects do not use cloud infrastructure and are unlikely to adopt it.
Log analysis tools (e.g., in JUnit) are of limited help without proper context.
The quality of an AI's answer is often proportional to the quality of the question and the amount of auxiliary knowledge available.
Incremental computation techniques have been replaced by materialized views in some contexts.
